welcome.title: Keep your website up to date with your latest experience
welcome.body: Sitetend watches your resume, profile and project notes, and suggests website updates with sources. You review, it writes, and every change can be undone.
empty.title: All caught up
empty.body: When you add a newer resume or change your materials, Sitetend suggests the matching website updates here.

external: The website files were changed outside Sitetend.

undo.leavePublished: After undoing, your local site will differ from the published version (the live site is not changed). Continue?
editTip: You can edit the suggestion before accepting.

saved: Saved to your website. You can undo it.

welcome.step1: Drop in your resume or project notes
welcome.step2: Review suggested changes, each with its source
welcome.step3: Apply in one click, undo any time
welcome.hint: You can also just say "add a new project" or "change my email to …"
err.PROVIDER_UNREACHABLE: Couldn't reach the AI model server. Check your internet connection, then try again.

sites.title: Websites
sites.removeTip: Remove from this list (no files are deleted)
sites.removed: Removed “{name}” from the list. No files were deleted.
sites.renameHint: Leave empty to use the site’s own name
tour.site.title: Your websites
tour.site.body: The website you are working on. Click to switch to another one or add a new folder; each keeps its own suggestions and history.
tour.materials.title: Your materials
tour.materials.body: Drag your résumé or notes into the dashed box (or click it). When they change, Sitetend suggests the website updates.
tour.check.title: Check for updates
tour.check.body: Sitetend checks on its own a few seconds after your materials change. Click here to check right away.
tour.card.title: A suggestion
tour.card.body: Each change comes with the line from your materials it is based on and a reason. Accept it, edit the text first, or reject it. Nothing changes until you accept.
tour.card.waiting: Making an example suggestion from the sample materials… Suggestions show up here, each with the line it is based on and a reason.
tour.card.none: Suggestions show up here, each with the line from your materials it is based on and a reason. Accept, edit or reject them; nothing changes until you accept.
tour.preview.title: Preview
tour.preview.body: Your website as it will look. Compare the change with the original or side by side, switch to phone width, or turn on “Edit text” to fix wording right on the page.
tour.undo.title: Undo and redo
tour.undo.body: Every change can be taken back, one step at a time. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z work too.
tour.chat.title: Ask Sitetend
tour.chat.body: Say what you want in your own words, like “add a new project” or “change my email to …”. Sitetend turns it into suggestions for you to review.
tour.publish.title: Publish
tour.publish.body: When everything looks right, publish here. The ⋯ menu next to it chooses how: push with Git, or mark it as published after you upload it yourself.

src.menuSub: Read materials from notes, drives or a CMS
hook.menuSub: Tell Slack, Discord or a script when something happens
src.intro: Sitetend can read materials you keep in another app (notes, a drive, a CMS) through that app's MCP server. What it reads is saved under sources/external/ in this website's folder and analysed like your other materials. Sources are read when you click "Check for updates", or on a schedule.
src.reading: Reading the sources and checking for updates…
src.removeConfirm: Remove the source "{name}"? Files already read stay in sources/external/ (delete them there if you no longer want them); its key is deleted.
src.name: Name
src.tokenEnv: Pass the key as environment variable
src.cmdSafety: The command runs on this computer with your permissions, like in a terminal. It is saved only in your Sitetend settings, never in the website folder, and agents connected over MCP cannot set it. Only use servers you trust.
src.keyPh: Leave empty if the server needs none
src.keyNote: Saved in ~/.sitetend/.env on this computer, sent only to this server.
src.connect: Connect and list what it offers
src.connected: Connected to {name}. Choose what to read:
src.connectFirst: Connect to see what the server offers.
src.toolsNote: A tool you pick is called each time the source is read. Prefer tools marked read-only.
src.badArgs: The arguments are not a JSON object.
src.nothing: This server offers no documents or tools.
src.noItems: Choose at least one document or tool (connect first).
src.syncFailed: Could not read: {names} (see Connect other services → External sources)
hook.intro: A webhook sends a short message to an address you choose when something happens in Sitetend: to Slack, Discord, an automation tool or your own server. Webhooks apply to every website.
hook.privacy: Messages say what happened and how many (e.g. "3 suggestions waiting"), never the content of your materials or website. Each one is signed (X-Sitetend-Signature, HMAC-SHA256 with the key below).
hook.secretNote: Your receiver can use it to check that a message really came from your Sitetend. Saved in ~/.sitetend/.env.
hook.inTitle: Let a script on this computer start a check
hook.inNote: For example after you export a new resume, from a git hook or a scheduled task. Only programs on this computer can reach it, and only with this key. It reads the external sources and checks for updates in the website that is open. The address stays the same while Sitetend uses the same port.
hook.ev.change.applied: A change was written to the website
hook.ev.sources.failed: An external source could not be read
hook.ev.analysis.failed: The AI model could not be reached
err.MCP_AUTH: The server refused the key (or needs one).

err.MCP_TIMEOUT: The server did not answer in time.

app.title: Open like an app
app.shortcutWhy: Create a Sitetend icon so you can open it with a double-click, with no terminal or .bat file. If Sitetend is already running, the icon just opens it.
app.shortcutDone.win: The Sitetend icon is on your desktop and in the Start menu. (If you move the Sitetend folder, create it again.)
app.shortcutDone.mac: Sitetend is in your Applications folder (in your home folder) and on the desktop. (If you move the Sitetend folder, create it again.)
app.shortcutDone.linux: Sitetend is in your app menu (and on the desktop, if you have one). (If you move the Sitetend folder, create it again.)
app.shortcutMade.win: Shortcut created on the desktop and in the Start menu.
app.shortcutMade.mac: Sitetend added to Applications and the desktop.
app.shortcutMade.linux: Sitetend added to the app menu.
app.welcomeShortcut: Create a desktop icon, then next time just double-click it
app.login: Start Sitetend when I sign in (in the background)
app.tray: Show an icon in the taskbar tray
app.trayNote: When Sitetend runs in the background, click the tray icon to open it, or right-click it to quit. Closing the browser tab does not stop Sitetend, so it keeps watching your materials.
app.trayOnlyWin: The tray icon is available on Windows. Here, open Sitetend again with its icon, and quit it with the button below.
app.quitConfirm: Quit Sitetend? It stops watching your materials until you open it again. Nothing is lost.
app.quitDoneSub: You can close this tab. Open Sitetend again with its icon.

help.title: Getting started: two questions
help.site.title: Your website folder
help.site.body: Choose the folder on your computer that holds your website's files (the one you upload or push to GitHub). If your website's words are in files in that folder, Sitetend works with it, however it was made. For example:
help.site.json: Text kept in a JSON file
help.site.no: Not supported: a website that lives only on an online builder (Wix, Squarespace, Notion), or whose words are kept in a database (WordPress).
help.mat.title: Your materials (what to drop in)
help.mat.body: Drop files onto the window, or use “Add files…”. A resume PDF, Markdown or text notes, and JSON all work (up to 20 MB each). Sitetend asks what each file is before using it.
help.mat.tip: Tip: write facts as “Label: value” lines, one per line. To update something, drop the newer version with the same file name. It replaces the old one (earlier versions are kept).
mat.dropHint: Drop a new résumé, portfolio or notes here
help.q1.title: 1. Which folder do I choose?
help.q1.body: The folder on your computer that holds your website: the one you upload to your web host or to GitHub.
help.q1.check: Quick check: inside it there is usually a file called index.html. Double-click it. If your website opens in the browser, it’s the right folder.
help.q1.unsure: Not sure? Choose the folder above it, or even Documents or Desktop. Sitetend looks inside and lists the websites it finds.
help.q1.no: Made your site with Wix, Squarespace, WordPress.com, Notion or another online site builder? Those sites live only online, so Sitetend can’t open or change them. Sitetend works with websites that are a folder of files on your computer.
help.q2.title: 2. What do I drop in?
help.q2.body: Anything that shows what’s new. Drag it into the dashed box on the left. For example:
help.q2.exampleLabel: A note can be as simple as this:
help.q2.example:
New job: Product Designer at Acme (since September 2026)
New email: alex@newmail.com
Finished project: Orbit Dock 1.7
help.q2.safe: Sitetend reads it and suggests changes to your website. Nothing changes until you click Accept, and every change can be undone.
find.title: Websites found in this folder
find.found: This folder isn’t a website itself, but Sitetend found {n} inside it. Open the one you want:
find.none: Sitetend looked inside this folder and found no website files (such as index.html). Try the folder you upload to your web host or GitHub, or look at a sample website first.
find.openedInside: Opened “{name}”, the website inside the folder you chose.
help.q2.i1: Your résumé or CV (PDF or Word)
help.q2.i2: Your portfolio, or a write-up of a project (PDF, Word or text)
help.q2.i3: A short note of what’s new (a plain text file, .txt or .md)
help.q2.i4: Your profile details as a JSON file, if you keep one
help.q2.chat: No file? Just type it in the chat box, like “Add my new job at Acme”. Notes kept in another app can be linked from the menu at the top left → Connect other services.
help.site.app: Astro, React, Next.js, Vue or Svelte project

mobile.tag: Your website, kept in sync with your materials.
mobile.about: Sitetend watches your resume, profile and project notes on your computer, and suggests website updates with sources. You review, it writes, and every change can be undone.
mobile.title: Please open Sitetend on a computer.
mobile.text: It works with the files on your computer and needs a larger screen to review changes side by side with your website.
skipped.banner: Sitetend cannot read {n} page(s), so no changes will be made there: {files}. A page can hold up to 2 MB of text (pictures in it do not count), and a site up to 1,000 pages.
skipped.encoding: Sitetend will not change {n} page(s) saved in an older text encoding (not UTF-8), so their characters stay intact: {files}. Save them as UTF-8 in your editor to let Sitetend update them.
preview.openLiveTip: The saved website as it runs in a browser, with its animations. Suggestions not yet accepted are not in it.
msg.recovered: Last time Sitetend was closed in the middle of saving. The changes you had accepted are now saved (see History; Undo takes them back).
backup.title: Backups
backup.on: Back up the whole website every day
backup.note: A .zip of the whole website folder (unzip it and you have the site), made before the first change of each day and when you open the site. The last 14 days are kept in your user folder, not in the website.
backup.confirm: The whole website goes back to how it was on {when}. Your current website is backed up first, so you can come back to it.
backup.restored: Website restored to {when}. It is in History and can be undone.
backup.failed: Today's backup could not be made: {message}
err.BACKUP_TOO_LARGE: The website is too large for a backup (over 3.5 GB or 60,000 files).
err.BACKUP_DAMAGED: This backup is damaged and was not used. The website was not changed.
err.BACKUP_NOT_FOUND: That backup is no longer there.
err.INTERNAL: Something went wrong inside Sitetend. Please try again; if it keeps happening, restart Sitetend.
publish.mode.cloudflare.sub: Publish uploads the website to your Cloudflare Pages project. Only changed files are sent.
publish.tip.cloudflare: Upload the website to your Cloudflare Pages project.
publish.manual.zipHint: To upload by hand, download the website as a .zip below and drag it into your host's upload page.
cf.step1: In Cloudflare, create an API token: Create Token → Create Custom Token, add the permission Account → Cloudflare Pages → Edit, then Continue and Create Token. Copy it (it is shown once) and paste it below.
cf.step2: Account ID: Cloudflare dashboard → Workers & Pages; it is shown on the right (32 letters and digits).
cf.step3: Project name: the name of your Pages project in that list (the part before .pages.dev).
cf.branchNote: Leave empty to update the live site. Any other name makes a preview at its own address.
err.CF_NO_TOKEN: No Cloudflare API token is saved yet. Open Cloudflare settings and paste one.
err.CF_BAD_ACCOUNT: The account ID should be 32 letters and digits. You find it in the Cloudflare dashboard under Workers & Pages.
err.CF_BAD_PROJECT: Enter the Pages project name as it appears in Cloudflare (letters, digits and dashes).
err.CF_NO_PROJECT: Cloudflare has no Pages project with this name in this account. Check the name under Workers & Pages.
err.CF_AUTH: Cloudflare did not accept the API token. Make sure it has the "Cloudflare Pages: Edit" permission for this account, or create a new one.
err.CF_NOT_FOUND: Cloudflare could not find the account or project. Check the account ID and project name.
err.CF_FAILED: Cloudflare refused the upload. Try again in a few minutes.
err.CF_NETWORK: Could not reach Cloudflare. Check the internet connection and try again.
err.CF_FUNCTIONS: This site uses Cloudflare Functions (a functions folder or _worker.js), which need Cloudflare's own tools to upload. Publish it with Git or wrangler instead.
err.CF_FILE_TOO_LARGE: {file} is larger than 25 MB, the limit for one file on Cloudflare Pages. Make it smaller or host it elsewhere.
publish.mode.netlify.sub: Publish uploads the website to your Netlify site. Only changed files are sent.
publish.tip.netlify: Upload the website to your Netlify site.
host.sub: Publish uploads your website straight to {host}, the same as uploading it in the {host} dashboard. Only changed files are sent.
host.tokenSaved: Saved (paste a new one to replace it)
host.folderNote: Leave empty to upload the website folder itself.
host.folderBuilt: Your site's build writes its pages to {folder}. Leave empty to use that.
host.checked: Connected to {name} ({url}). {n} files will be uploaded.
host.confirm: Upload the website ({n} files) to {name} on {host}? Your live site will update. Your materials and Sitetend's data are not included.
host.confirmPreview: Upload the website ({n} files) to {name} on {host} as a preview? Your live site does not change.
host.done: Published to {host} ({total} files; {n} changed and were uploaded). {url}
host.donePreview: Preview uploaded to {host} ({total} files; {n} changed and were uploaded). {url}
nl.step1: In Netlify, open User settings → Applications → Personal access tokens, create a token and paste it below.
nl.step2: Site: the address of your site (for example mysite.netlify.app), its custom domain, or its Project ID.
nl.siteNote: Just the name works too: mysite means mysite.netlify.app.
nl.draftNote: The live site does not change. You get a separate preview address.
err.PUB_TOO_MANY_FILES: The website has more files than this host allows in one upload.
err.PUB_EMPTY: There are no files to upload in this folder.
err.PUB_FOLDER_MISSING: The folder to upload does not exist yet. If your site has a build step, let it finish first, or check the folder in the publish settings.
err.PUB_FOLDER_OUTSIDE: The folder to upload must be inside the website folder.
err.PUB_BUILD_FAILED: The last build failed, so the uploaded site would be out of date. Fix the build first.
err.NL_NO_TOKEN: No Netlify access token is saved yet. Open the Netlify settings and paste one.
err.NL_BAD_SITE: Enter the site address, for example mysite.netlify.app, or its Project ID.
err.NL_NO_SITE: This Netlify account has no site at that address. Check the address in Netlify under Projects.
err.NL_AUTH: Netlify did not accept the access token. It may have expired; create a new one.
err.NL_FORBIDDEN: This access token is not allowed to change that site. Use a token from the account that owns it.
err.NL_NOT_FOUND: Netlify could not find the site. Check the site address.
err.NL_RATE: Netlify allows 3 uploads a minute. Wait a moment and publish again.
err.NL_FAILED: Netlify could not finish the upload. Try again in a few minutes.
err.NL_NETWORK: Could not reach Netlify. Check the internet connection and try again.
err.NL_FUNCTIONS: This site has Netlify Functions, which need Netlify's own tools to upload. Publish it with Git or the Netlify CLI instead.
err.NL_BAD_NAME: Netlify cannot take a file whose name contains # or ?: {file}. Rename it first.
err.NL_SLOW: Netlify is taking unusually long to finish. Check the site in Netlify; it may still go live.
mem.title: Memory
mem.note: What you asked Sitetend to keep in mind. A model sees only the notes that fit the work at hand. You can change, pause or remove any of them.
mem.none: Nothing yet. Say "from now on…" in the conversation, or add a note here.
mem.from.question: Your answer
mem.add.ph: For example: Write job titles in English.
mem.saved: Remembered. You can change it in Settings → Advanced → Memory.
mem.followedGone: Following a note you have since removed.
mem.ask.title: Remember this?
mem.ask.body: You made the same change to {n} suggestions:
mem.rule.month-short: Write months in short form ({to}, not {from}).
mem.rule.no-end-period: No full stop at the end of short lines.
mem.rule.end-period: End short lines with a full stop.
mem.text.notYet: Not yet: do not put "{value}" ({label}) on the website until I say so.
mem.text.private: Do not put "{value}" ({label}) on the website.
why.title: Why not? (optional)
why.sub: About: {label}. Your answer helps next time; skip it if you like.
err.MEMORY_FULL: The memory is full. Remove some notes first.
err.MEMORY_BAD: This note could not be saved.
cf.tokenLink: Open the token page (permission already chosen)
preview.scriptDrawn: This page is mostly drawn by the site's own scripts (a video, a canvas or an app), and the preview does not run scripts, so it looks empty here. Its words can still be suggested and changed.
preview.openLiveChange: Open in browser with this change
preview.openLiveChangeTip: The real page, with its own scripts running, with this suggestion in place and its words highlighted. Nothing is saved.
preview.liveBanner: Sitetend: suggested change shown, not saved yet ({label}). Highlighted where it appears.
preview.liveOn: Live preview: this page runs its own scripts, as in a browser (Sitetend stays out of its reach).
preview.liveOnChange: Live preview with this suggestion in place (not saved yet); the changed words are highlighted.
preview.part: {part} is a part of {host}: that page loads it with its scripts, so it is shown inside {host}, live. Open "{name}" in the site below to see it.
preview.partChange: This suggestion is in {part}, a part of {host}. It is shown inside {host}, live and not saved yet: open "{name}" in the site below; the changed words are highlighted.
preview.editPart: {host} is drawn by its own scripts, so its words are edited on its parts: this is {part}, as it is without {host} around it (the layout can differ from the website). Pick another part at the top right.
preview.reloadTip: Load the page again (after you change files yourself)
preview.editBlank: {page} needs the website's own scripts to show its content, so it is blank while editing and its words can't be edited in place. Pick another page at the top right, or ask Sitetend in the chat to change a word.
card.copies: The same words are also in {files}; accepting changes them there too.
item.picKept: the picture of the copied entry
item.warn.link: {field}: no link yet, left as # (the copied entry linked to {value}).
code.check: Code written by the AI model. Look at it in the preview before you accept; you can undo it.
preview.partBlank: {part} also needs the website's own scripts to show its content, so it is blank here and its words can't be edited in place. Pick another part at the top right, or ask Sitetend in the chat to change a word.
